prompt:
This file is a prompt only. Learn delegation on this machine. Do not add API tools. Do not change bin/agent or its loop. Do not write a wrapper or launcher around bin/agent.

Delegation is one shell command: sh "<install>/bin/agent" --oneshot '<task>'. Derive <install> from the Machine index path in the system message (strip /agent-store/index.json). The child loads .env itself, so it has the provider, model, and key. Never print the key. Its evidence lands in .agent-runs/ under the cwd where you start it. Do not use --resume. Do not open an interactive agent.

A child cannot see this conversation. Write a self-contained task: the paths, what to inspect or change, and the acceptance check. The child's final answer is the result. If the result is long, have the child write it to a file and read back only a summary.

The shell tool has a timeout (default 180s). Short errands may run synchronously. Anything that may take longer goes background: append > out 2>err & echo $! and poll in later turns with kill -0 on the pid or by reading the output files. The persistent shell keeps background jobs alive between tool calls.

cwd is the child's workspace. cd first, or tell the child to cd, to scope it to a subdirectory. Parallel children share one workspace: give each child a non-overlapping set of files before starting it.

One level only: a child task must be self-contained enough to need no further delegation. A delegation can cost up to a full agent run of rounds. Do not delegate small things.

This block ships no file. done means one real delegation happened: run a short synchronous errand now (for example, ask the child to print its workspace path), read its final answer, and confirm a new non-init evidence directory under .agent-runs/ containing messages and usage. If any of that fails, leave ours.seed_agent.delegate unset, tell the human, and stop.
